exposure: Mode of delivery (elective cesarean delivery vs. uncomplicated vaginal delivery)
cohort: 517 women who delivered 6 years prior to the study (309 with uncomplicated vaginal deliveries and 208 with elective cesarean deliveries)
finding: Six years postpartum, uncomplicated vaginal delivery was associated with urinary incontinence, while elective cesarean delivery was associated with sexual and urination pain.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean delivery was associated with significantly less urgency urinary incontinence and stress incontinence compared to uncomplicated vaginal delivery.
